findings.summary: Per-arm chronology allowed postfreeze material to open before the remaining arms had frozen while the final batch still passed.
A prefreeze-safe dispatch ZIP now excludes mapping, custody, scorer, score-sheet, and threshold material; postfreeze material remains in a separate ZIP.
One atomic lock binds four exact finalized responses, four distinct responder IDs, a distinct collector ID, timestamps, bundle hashes, packet hashes, dispatch bytes, and commitment bytes.
The postfreeze scorer revalidates each complete triplet and rejects current response bytes, identities, or finalization times that disagree with the prefreeze response-set lock.
A valid-shaped lock placed after custody opening is hash-bound into the run manifest and rejected by the final scorer.
ZIP members and filesystem JSON now share one strict UTF-8, duplicate-key, and non-finite-number parser.
The ordinary validation toolchain executes the staged four-arm pilot and all seven negative canaries.
No genuine external four-response lock/batch or conventional OQ-0266 triplet exists; local clocks and string IDs are not trusted time or identity proof.

next_action: Run the prefreeze dispatch kit with four genuinely separate responders, freeze the exact all-response lock, then open the postfreeze kit and preserve the complete evidence package.
non_claim: This observation file is not external evidence, identity proof, trusted timestamping, causal burden evidence, compact-default confirmation, or canonical promotion.
